content_of_post_to_comment: Yesterday, I watched as one of our new students (3rd grade) grew frustrated with her math (adding three one-digit numbers) because she’s not fluent in her basic addition facts. Every problem required her to count on her fingers. Later in the day, I had to ask her to stop singing the lyrics to an inappropriate song during class (which she had memorized completely). The idea that students can’t or shouldn’t memorize math facts is just about the dumbest, most absurd notion I’ve ever heard. When we act as if they can’t memorize them, we convey our expectations. When we say they shouldn’t memorize we fail to help them build fluency which leads to frustration. Kids memorize all sorts of things. (Some of which I wish they didn’t.) Math facts should hold a spot in their memory bank. That shouldn’t be controversial.
